entities.summary:
Jan II van Wassenaer (1483-1523) was a prominent Dutch nobleman, admiral, and stadtholder of Holland during a pivotal period of early modern European history, marked by the consolidation of Habsburg power and the burgeoning maritime influence of the Low Countries. His career spanned the final decades of the Burgundian Netherlands and the early years of Habsburg rule under Philip the Handsome and Charles V, making him a key figure in the political and military administration of the region. He inherited the prestigious titles of Lord of Wassenaer and Burggraaf (Viscount) of Leiden, placing him at the apex of the regional nobility and connecting him to centuries of Dutch aristocratic lineage.

Wassenaer distinguished himself primarily through military service and administrative leadership. In 1500, he was appointed Admiral of Holland, a crucial role in protecting Dutch shipping interests and projecting naval power in the North Sea. He commanded fleets against Danish and Hanseatic League forces, notably participating in the Guelders Wars and the conflicts against the pirates of the Frisian coast, securing vital trade routes. As stadtholder of Holland (1515-1521), he served as the highest representative of the Habsburg sovereign, responsible for maintaining order, administering justice, and raising taxes and troops, navigating the complex political landscape of the Estates of Holland during a period of increasing centralisation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jan II van Wassenaer was a significant regional figure whose military and administrative leadership contributed to the stability of Holland during the early period of Habsburg rule, laying groundwork for later Dutch state and naval development. His career exemplifies the evolving role of the nobility in the Low Countries.
